claims.text: Reversible, thermally activated local microstructural transformations occur in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed transformations may consist of transient short-range ordering or nanoscale phase separation.
Local microstructural transformations create spatial variations in thermal expansion.
Spatially varying thermal expansion generates intrinsic stress fields.
The intrinsic stress fields modulate tensile-creep behavior.
The intrinsic stress fields modulate microhardness evolution during cold rolling.
The intrinsic stress fields modulate the temperature dependence of elastic moduli.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is single-phase and fully homogenized.
Thermal cycling or aging at 600–800 °C induces local microstructural ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated local reordering produces local lattice-parameter variations.
Aged or thermally cycled samples will have greater spatial heterogeneity in lattice parameters than fully homogenized samples.
Aged or thermally cycled samples will have greater spatial heterogeneity in local elastic moduli than fully homogenized samples.
Aging or thermal cycling will alter the tensile-creep rate at 1250 °C relative to a fully homogenized baseline.
Aging or thermal cycling will modify the thermoelastic response relative to a fully homogenized baseline.
The proposed effects become strong above approximately 600 °C and are most pronounced at 1250 °C.
A fully homogenized HfNbTaTiZr baseline has uniform lattice parameters.
Existing studies show generally that microstructural evolution can accompany and influence mechanical behavior in high-entropy alloys.
A related NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 refractory alloy exhibits temperature-dependent tensile strength and work-hardening followed by softening at elevated temperature.
